exists when a person occupies with the owner's consent but with no fixed term and no agreed periodic term — possession continues at the will of both parties and may be ended by either. Lacking both a fixed end date and automatic renewal, it is the estate most likely to be created by accident: an owner lets a relative move in with no agreement about rent or duration, or a seller lets a buyer take possession informally before closing. The distinction matters, because chapter 92's protections attach to a "tenant," defined in § 92.001(6) as "a person who is authorized by a lease to occupy a dwelling to the exclusion of others and, for the purposes of Subchapters D, E, and F, who is obligated under the lease to pay rent." Read the whole definition: for the security-device, disclosure-of-ownership, and smoke-alarm subchapters, the occupant must also be obligated by the lease to pay rent, so an authorized occupant who owes no rent is not a "tenant" for those three subchapters even though he is one elsewhere in the chapter. And § 92.001(3) counts an oral understanding as a lease.

existe cuando una persona ocupa con el consentimiento del propietario pero sin plazo fijo y sin plazo periódico convenido — la posesión continúa a voluntad de ambas partes y puede ser terminada por cualquiera de ellas. Al carecer tanto de una fecha límite fija como de renovación automática, es el patrimonio más probable que se cree por accidente: un propietario deja que un familiar se mude sin acuerdo sobre el alquiler o la duración, o un vendedor deja que un comprador tome posesión informalmente antes de cerrar. La distinción importa, porque las protecciones del capítulo 92 se refieren a un "teniente", definido en el § 92.001(6) como "una persona que está autorizada por un contrato de arrendamiento para ocupar una vivienda con la exclusión de otros y, a los efectos de los subcapítulos D, E y F, que está obligada en virtud del contrato de arrendamiento a pagar el alquiler". Lea la definición completa: para el dispositivo de seguridad, la revelación de propiedad, y los subcapítulos de alarma de humo, el ocupante también debe estar obligado por el contrato de arrendamiento a pagar el alquiler, por lo que un autorizado ocupante que no debe alquiler no es un "teniente" para esos tres subcapítulos, a pesar de que es uno en otra parte del capítulo. Y § 92.001(3) cuenta un entendimiento oral como un contrato de arrendamiento.

improvements, four conditions attach, and they are the reason a Texas home-improvement lien is a formal transaction rather than a handshake: (A) the work and material must be "contracted for in writing, with the consent of both spouses, in the case of a family homestead, given in the same manner as is required in making a sale and conveyance of the homestead"; (B) the contract must not be "executed by the owner or the owner's spouse before the fifth day after the owner makes written application for any extension of credit for the work and material"; (C) the contract must "expressly provide[] that the owner may rescind the contract without penalty or charge within three days after the execution of the contract by all parties"; and (D) the contract must be "executed by the owner and the owner's spouse only at the office of a third-party lender making an extension of credit for the work and material, an attorney at law, or a title company." Conditions (B) and (C) both yield where "the work and material are necessary to complete immediate repairs to conditions on the homestead property that materially affect the health or safety of the owner or person residing in the homestead and the owner of the homestead acknowledges such in writing." That emergency carve-out is the Constitution recognizing that a family with a failed roof cannot wait five days.

is a final payment substantially larger than the periodic payments preceding it, arising because the payment schedule was not designed to retire the debt over the term. A loan amortized on a thirty-year schedule but due in seven years will have twenty-three years of principal left outstanding when the note matures, and that remainder is the balloon. Balloons are not inherently abusive — they are ordinary in commercial lending — but on a home loan they place the borrower in a position of having to refinance or sell on a date fixed years in advance, regardless of what interest rates or property values are doing that month.

In Texas this analysis is genuinely local. An appraiser working the Permian Basin is analyzing an economy whose housing demand tracks the rig count; an appraiser in Austin is analyzing an economy whose demand tracks technology employment and a constrained supply of developable land; an appraiser in the Rio Grande Valley is analyzing a different market again. is one that takes deposits from the public and lends a portion of those deposits out. Commercial banks, savings institutions, and credit unions are depositories. The defining feature, for our purposes, is that a depository has its own balance sheet of customer deposits available as a funding source. It can originate a loan and fund it with money that is already sitting inside the institution, and if it chooses, it can keep that loan on its own books — hold it "in portfolio" — collect the payments itself, and never involve anyone else. When a depository holds a loan in portfolio it has originated, funded, and serviced the loan, and the borrower deals with one name from application through payoff.

es una que toma depósitos del público y presta una porción de esos depósitos. Los bancos comerciales, las instituciones de ahorro y las cooperativas de crédito son depositarios. Puede originar un préstamo y financiarlo con dinero que ya está sentado dentro de la institución, y si lo elige, puede mantener ese préstamo en sus propios libros — mantenerlo "en cartera" — recoger los pagos en sí mismo, y nunca involucrar a nadie más. Cuando un depositario tiene un préstamo en cartera se ha originado, financiado y atendido el préstamo, y el prestatario se ocupa de un nombre de la aplicación a través de pago.

is where loans that already exist are bought and sold. No borrower participates in it. Its participants are the institutions that originated loans and want to sell them, and the investors who want to own the income stream those loans produce. A loan that is sold in the secondary market does not change: the borrower still owes the same principal at the same rate on the same schedule, secured by the same lien on the same Texas property. What changes is who owns the right to be paid.

es donde se compran y venden los préstamos que ya existen. Ningún prestatario participa en ella. Sus participantes son las instituciones que originaron los préstamos y quieren venderlos, y los inversores que quieren poseer la corriente de ingresos que producen esos préstamos. Un préstamo que se vende en el mercado secundario no cambia: el prestatario todavía debe el mismo principal a la misma tasa en el mismo horario, asegurado por el mismo gravamen en la misma propiedad de Texas. Lo que cambia es quién tiene el derecho a ser pagado.

is worth stating precisely, because it is the classic examination distinction. Insurance is a policy under which the insurer pays the lender's covered loss; the borrower pays a premium for it. A guaranty is a promise by a third party to answer for part of the borrower's debt if the borrower does not pay; the guaranteed portion is expressed as an amount or fraction of the loan rather than as an insurance policy. In practical effect both reduce the lender's exposure, which is why both support financing terms a lender would not otherwise offer. In legal form they are different instruments.

vale la pena decir con precisión, porque es la distinción de examen clásico. El seguro es una póliza bajo la cual el asegurador paga la pérdida cubierta del prestamista; el prestatario paga una prima por ella. Una garantía es una promesa de un tercero de responder por una parte de la deuda del prestatario si el prestatario no paga; la porción garantizada se expresa como una cantidad o fracción del préstamo en lugar de como una póliza de seguro. En efecto, ambos reducen la exposición del prestamista, por lo que ambas condiciones de financiación de apoyo un prestamista no ofrecería de otra manera. En su forma jurídica son instrumentos diferentes.

more broadly is any provision raising rent on a stated trigger — a fixed annual step-up, an index adjustment, or a pass-through of increases in a defined expense. Texas law notices this last variety in one narrow place: Property Code § 92.332(a)(1) provides that a landlord is not liable for retaliation for "increasing rent under an escalation clause in a written lease for utilities, taxes, or insurance." That provision does not authorize escalation clauses — the lease does — but it confirms that such a clause is a legitimate reason for a rent increase and not evidence of retaliation.

of the most probable price a property should bring in a competitive and open market, under conditions that make a sale fair, with buyer and seller each acting prudently and knowledgeably, each typically motivated, neither under duress, both well informed, payment made in cash or its equivalent, and the price unaffected by special financing or concessions. Every clause in that formulation is doing work. "Most probable," not highest possible or lowest acceptable. "Competitive and open market" — the property was exposed for a reasonable time. "Typically motivated" and "neither under duress" — this excludes the forced sale and the desperate buyer. "Unaffected by special financing" — a seller who buys down the buyer's interest rate by $14,000 has effectively discounted the price, and the recorded number overstates value by roughly that amount. A common error is to treat the most recent sale price of a nearly identical house as market value without asking whether that sale satisfied these conditions. Often it did not.

on three restrictions. Both forbid balloon payments on a covered loan, and both carve out seasonal or irregular income and bridge loans — but the lines are drawn differently. The federal rule at § 1026.32(d)(1) bars any payment "more than two times a regular periodic payment," full stop; Finance Code § 343.202 bars a payment "more than twice as large as the average of earlier scheduled monthly payments, unless the balloon payment becomes due not less than 60 months after the date of the loan." Texas permits a late balloon; the federal rule does not condition the prohibition on timing at all. Both forbid negative amortization in nearly identical words — compare § 1026.32(d)(2) with Finance Code § 343.203 — though Texas adds its own exception for negative amortization arising from "a temporary forbearance, bridge loan, or restructure sought by the borrower." And both forbid prepayment penalties: § 1026.32(d)(6) as a prohibited term, Finance Code § 343.205 as a flat statutory bar.

plan starts with a payment lower than a fully amortizing payment and increases it on a predetermined schedule — typically each year for a set number of years — until it reaches a level that fully amortizes the remaining balance over the remaining term. The design serves a borrower who expects income to rise. The risk is structural: in the early years the scheduled payment may be less than the interest accruing, and when that happens the shortfall is added to the principal.

El plan comienza con un pago inferior a un pago totalmente amortizador y lo aumenta en un calendario predeterminado, normalmente cada año durante un número determinado de años, hasta que alcanza un nivel que amortiza totalmente el saldo restante durante el resto del período. El diseño sirve a un prestatario que espera que los ingresos aumenten. runs from period to period — month to month is the common Texas residential form, though week to week and year to year are also periodic — renewing automatically at the end of each period until one party gives notice. No ending date is fixed at the outset. Chapter 91, which supplies rules applicable to landlords and tenants generally, governs how a Texas month-to-month tenancy ends. Section 91.001(a): "A monthly tenancy or a tenancy from month to month may be terminated by the tenant or the landlord giving notice of termination to the other." Either side may end it; neither needs cause. Section 91.001(b) fixes the effective date: "If a notice of termination is given under Subsection (a) and if the rent-paying period is at least one month, the tenancy terminates on whichever of the following days is the later: (1) the day given in the notice for termination; or (2) one month after the day on which the notice is given." Where the rent-paying period is shorter than a month, § 91.001(c) substitutes a period equal in days to the rent-paying period.

Al principio no se fija ninguna fecha de finalización. El capítulo 91, que provee reglas aplicables a los terratenientes e inquilinos en general, gobierna cómo termina un alquiler mes a mes en Texas. unit sets them out from 12 C.F.R. § 1026.32(a)(1) in full. In short form: a transaction secured by the consumer's principal dwelling is a high-cost mortgage if its annual percentage rate exceeds the average prime offer rate for a comparable transaction by more than 6.5 percentage points on most first liens, or 8.5 percentage points on a subordinate lien or on a first lien where the dwelling is personal property and the loan amount is under $50,000; or if total points and fees exceed 5 percent of the total loan amount on a loan of $20,000 or more (the $20,000 adjusts annually by CPI); or if the creditor can charge a prepayment penalty more than 36 months after consummation or penalties totaling more than 2 percent of the amount prepaid. Texas then narrows the field further with its own principal-amount ceiling in § 343.201(1)(C) and its own $20,000 floor and rate-or-fee alternative in § 343.201(1)(E). A loan can therefore be a federal high-cost mortgage without being a Texas high-cost home loan, because the Texas category is capped at one-half the maximum conventional first-mortgage loan amount and the federal category is not.

En forma abreviada: una transacción garantizada por la vivienda principal del consumidor es una hipoteca de alto costo si su tasa porcentual anual excede la tasa de oferta primaria media para una transacción comparable en más de 6.5 puntos porcentuales en la mayoría de los primeros gravámenes, o 8.5 puntos porcentuales en un gravamen subordinado o en un primer gravamen donde la vivienda es propiedad personal y el monto del préstamo está por debajo de $50,000; o si el total de puntos y honorarios excede 5 por ciento del monto total del préstamo en un préstamo de $20,000 o más (el $20,000 se ajusta anualmente por CPI); o si el acreedor puede cobrar una multa por prepago más de 36 meses después de la consumación o sanciones totalizando más de 2 por ciento de la cantidad pagada. Texas luego estrecha el campo con su propio techo principal en § 343.201(1)(C) y su propio piso y tarifa de $20,000 alternativa en § 343.201(1)(E). Por lo tanto, un préstamo puede ser una hipoteca federal de alto costo sin ser un préstamo hipotecario de alto costo de Texas, porque la categoría de Texas está limitada a la mitad de la cantidad máxima de préstamo convencional de primera hipoteca y la categoría federal no lo está.

— "an owelty of partition imposed against the entirety of the property by a court order or by a written agreement of the parties to the partition, including a debt of one spouse in favor of the other spouse resulting from a division or an award of a family homestead in a divorce proceeding" (§ 50(a)(3)). Owelty is the payment one co-owner makes to another to equalize a division of jointly owned property. The clause matters constantly in Texas divorce practice: the spouse awarded the house owes the other spouse for that spouse's share, and this is the provision that lets the obligation be secured by the homestead itself.

— "una deuda de partición impuesta contra la totalidad de la propiedad por una orden judicial o por un acuerdo escrito de las partes en la partición, incluyendo una deuda de un cónyuge a favor del otro cónyuge resultante de una división o una adjudicación de una casa de familia en un procedimiento de divorcio" (§ 50(a)(3)). Owelty es el pago que un copropietario hace a otro para igualar una división de propiedad conjunta. La cláusula importa constantemente en la práctica del divorcio en Texas: el cónyuge a quien se le concedió la casa debe al otro cónyuge por la parte de ese cónyuge, y esta es la disposición que permite que la obligación sea asegurada por la propia casa.

A lien that could validly attach may be refinanced, and the refinancing lien takes the place of the lien it retires. Subsection (e) polices the boundary: a refinance of debt described by subsections (a)(1) through (a)(5) "that includes the advance of additional funds may not be secured by a valid lien against the homestead" unless the refinance is itself a section 50(a)(6) extension of credit, or "the advance of all the additional funds is for reasonable costs necessary to refinance such debt or for a purpose described by Subsection (a)(2), (a)(3), or (a)(5)." In plain terms: you may refinance what was validly owed, and you may add closing costs and taxes and owelty and construction money — but the moment cash goes into the borrower's pocket, the loan has become a home equity loan and must satisfy every condition of section 50(a)(6).

— a section not held — and in doing so sets out what a defendant who acquired property after the disposal must establish, including that "[a]t the time the defendant acquired the facility the defendant did not know and had no reason to know that any hazardous substance which is the subject of the release or threatened release was disposed of on, in, or at the facility." Section 9601(35)(B)(i) explains "reason to know": the person must show that "on or before the date on which the defendant acquired the facility" it "carried out all appropriate inquiries, as provided in clauses (ii) and (iv), into the previous ownership and uses of the facility in accordance with generally accepted good commercial and customary standards and practices" — the inquiries are the ones those clauses define, not whatever inquiry the buyer thought sufficient — and took reasonable steps to stop any continuing release, prevent any threatened future release, and prevent or limit exposure to any previously released hazardous substance. Section 9601(35)(B)(iii) then lists the criteria the Administrator must include in the standards, and the list reads like a due-diligence checklist written by Congress: the results of an inquiry by an environmental professional; interviews with past and present owners, operators, and occupants; reviews of historical sources "such as chain of title documents, aerial photographs, building department records, and land use records"; searches for recorded environmental cleanup liens; reviews of federal, state, and local government records, waste disposal records, underground storage tank records, and spill records; "[v]isual inspections of the facility and of adjoining properties"; the person's specialized knowledge or experience; "[t]he relationship of the purchase price to the value of the property, if the property was not contaminated"; commonly known or reasonably ascertainable information; and the obviousness of contamination. Section 9601(35)(B)(iv)(II) names the interim standard for property purchased on or after May 31, 1997 and until the Administrator's regulations issue: the ASTM procedures, "including the document known as 'Standard E1527–97', entitled 'Standard Practice for Environmental Site Assessment: Phase 1 Environmental Site Assessment Process'", which the clause says shall satisfy its requirements. And § 9601(35)(B)(v) is the residential rule: for property in residential or similar use purchased by a nongovernmental or noncommercial entity, "a facility inspection and title search that reveal no basis for further investigation" satisfies the subparagraph.

Sección 9601(35) B) iii) luego enumera los criterios que el Administrador debe incluir en las normas, y la lista se lee como una lista de verificación de debida diligencia escrita por el Congreso: los resultados de una investigación por un profesional ambiental; entrevistas con propietarios, operadores y ocupantes pasados y presentes; revisiones de fuentes históricas "como la cadena de documentos de título, fotografías aéreas, registros de departamentos de construcción, y registros de uso de la tierra"; búsquedas para derechos de limpieza ambiental registrados; revisiones de federal, estado, y registros del gobierno local, registros de eliminación de desechos, registros de tanques de almacenamiento subterráneos y registros de derrames; "inspecciones [v]isuales de la instalación y de las propiedades adyacentes"; los conocimientos especializados o la experiencia de la persona; "la relación del precio de compra con el valor de la propiedad, si la propiedad no estaba contaminada"; información comúnmente conocida o razonablemente determinable; y la obvia contaminación. Sección 9601(35)B)iv)II) designa la norma provisional para los bienes adquiridos a partir de mayo 31, 1997 y hasta la emisión de reglamentos del Administrador: los procedimientos ASTM, "incluyendo el documento conocido como 'Norma E1527–97', titulado 'Práctica estándar para la evaluación ambiental de los emplazamientos: fase 1 Proceso de Evaluación Ambiental de Sitios'", que la cláusula dice que cumplirá con sus requisitos. — el término Código Financiero § 343.201(1)(E) préstamos — significa "una transacción en la que una hipoteca, escritura de fideicomisario, garantía monetaria de compra derivada de un contrato de venta a plazos, o garantías consensuales equivalentes se crean o retienen en la vivienda principal del consumidor para financiar la adquisición o construcción inicial de dicha vivienda" (§ 1026.2(a)(24)). Se trata de una transacción de compra-dinero o de construcción inicial, no de una refinanciación y no de un préstamo de capital.

— who pays which of the property's operating costs, and how the rent is computed. These categories are commercial practice and market vocabulary rather than Texas statutory definitions; no held Texas source defines "triple net" or "percentage lease," and you should present them to a client as customary terms whose meaning comes from the lease document itself, never from a statute. That caution is not academic: two landlords in the same market can use "net lease" to mean two different cost splits. Always read the expense clauses.

— quién paga cuál de los gastos de explotación de la propiedad, y cómo se calcula el alquiler. Estas categorías son la práctica comercial y el vocabulario de mercado en lugar de las definiciones legales de Texas; ninguna fuente de Texas detentada define "triple red" o "alquiler porcentual", y usted debe presentarlas a un cliente como términos habituales cuyo significado proviene del propio documento de arrendamiento, nunca de una ley. Esa precaución no es académica: dos propietarios en el mismo mercado pueden usar el "arrendamiento neto" para significar dos escisiones de costos diferentes. Siempre lea las cláusulas de gastos.
